notes.title: Lila’s Sky Ark Available NOW!
notes.notes:
Hello Skyward Adventurers,

The wait is finally over, and your mysterious journey through Lila’s psychedelic 
world is about to begin! 

Graffiti Games and Monolith of Minds are pleased to finally announce that Lila’s Sky 
Ark launches TODAY. Check out our launch trailer below for a sneak peek at what 
awaits you along Lila’s journey.

[previewyoutube=0T5QEnMAk_Q;full][Lila’s Sky Ark Launch Trailer (Steam Version)][/previewyoutube]

Help Lila clear the fog obscuring her past by unraveling her puzzle-like story in this 
lyrical action-adventure game. Along the way, you’ll explore a vibrant and musical 
world full of eccentric friends, bizarre beasts, and punishing bosses as you strive to 
prevent the Conductor and his minions from destroying all things musical and 
magical. Seek out alchemy recipes to unlock new weapons. Battle enemies and 
punishing bosses with rocks, Titan Eyes, cluster bombs, and anything else you can 
throw at them as you wander this music-inspired pixel dreamscape during Lila’s 
strange yet beautiful journey.

This game is filled with music and mystery, and Lila needs your help to figure out 
what’s going on. We urge you not to keep the lady waiting!

We can’t wait for you to dive in and let us know what you think. To stay in touch 
and up-to-date on all things Lila, follow Monolith of Minds on [url=https://twitter.com/monolithofminds]Twitter[/url] and [url=https://discord.com/invite/uAkZgBp7gz]Discord[/url], and for more great games, be sure to follow Graffiti Games on [url=https://twitter.com/Graffiti_Games]Twitter[/url] and [url=https://discord.io/graffitigames]Discord[/url] as well.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40056258/489f9ad014a428bdc0650b5596f60a1b2538a073.gif[/img]

See you in the sky!

Cheers,
The Lila’s Sky Ark Team and Graffiti Games

notes.title: Demo of Lila’s Sky Ark is Out!
notes.notes:
Hello impatient worshipers of the pineal gland,

Don’t read this newsletter. Instead go to Steam and download the [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1573390/Lilas_Sky_Ark/]demo of Lila’s Sky Ark[/url] right now! We promise 45 minutes of celestial sheep, the Wisp King, and magic.
Also, it’s free.

Since you’re back already, let's remind you this is, Views from the Monolith, our chaotic newsletter filled with adventures in the world of video game development (and occasionally consumption).

Steam is hosting its #NEXTFEST with lots of fresh demos, starting today. Over the last weeks we took a detour from our roadmap to splice together some preexisting content of Lila’s Sky Ark. We promise to go on the gamedev-journey together and having you dig into it as soon as possible is crucial.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40056258/475e856f1ebd3a3df0d7d8ef7352c3e513514145.png[/img]

This demo should give you a pretty good idea of how we want Lila’s Sky Ark to feel— pick-up and throw mechanics are in place, an early stretch of the story is laid out, and the first mini boss is waiting for you to challenge him.

If you get the chance to download and play the demo, we would love to hear from you. Did you enjoy it? Does it get you excited for the full game? Does it come up to your expectations? Please reach out directly via the in-demo feedback or [url=https://discord.gg/uAkZgBp7gz]visit our Discord[/url] and let us know what we can improve. After all, we’re crafting this video game for you.

[h1]The Mountain[/h1]

Besides putting together the demo we also made some massive progress on the overall game over the last weeks. Not only did we finish the first major boss (no spoilers, yet), but we also made substantial headway on the second biome of Lila’s sky-island: the Mountain.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40056258/d436441ae963a61ef8b25546c0651728173f0764.png[/img]

Here, in the realm of the Spirit Elephant, queen bees breed tiny bees, priests meditate to rhythm of the field, and rock giants do what rock giants do: they insult you.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40056258/61f1dcfed8e5f79aaf94b93b806f3b9add2307e5.png[/img]

Since the core mechanics should be established when reaching the mountain, battles will be more nasty, puzzles more mind-boggling, and encounters and dialogs as ridiculous as we get away with.

[h1]Robot Graveyard Design Process[/h1]

Speaking about ridiculous encounters: last month we expanded the forest by an area called the, “Robot Graveyard.” Since many of you have asked us about our pixel-design workflow, we recorded the whole four hour session, and compressed it [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iF1d79UJUAA]into a 30 minute video[/url].
Enjoy.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40056258/021c913b1fcac69230cecc8ec323b09675b4ff34.png[/img]

[h1]Resolutiion’s Birthday, Encore[/h1]

The last piece of news for this newsletter is another goody as nostalgic as it gets: Richi rummaged through the archive, digging up Resolutiion’s very first build, when it was still called Red Wars.
It’s bad, buggy, and ugly, but awesome to see how far we have come since those early days. What also struck us was, how much we kept from this initial prototype, regarding architecture and level design.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40056258/c8a2d36ba46ba0048a080b6ce78bde38c11037cc.png[/img]

[url=https://resolutiion.itch.io/red-wars]Download Red Wars v0.00001 at itch.io[/url] for Windows and Linux, and try to reach its end without crashing the build. There’s also a speed-run competition happening on MoM’s Discord server, so feel free compare your time with the community.

Thanks for reaching the end of this newsletter. May your pineal gland receive cosmic enlightenment.

Bye for now.

notes.title: Of Dinosaur Forests and German Awards
notes.notes:
Hello lovely, button-mashing monkeys with exceptionally large brains,

This is “Views from the Monolith,” our infrequent newsletter (on Steam or your inbox) filled with our adventures in the world of video games. Let’s dive right in.

With everything we learned during Resolutiion’s creation, we have formed better processes. Development has become more structured and efficient, and for the last four months, we’ve been ahead of our own roadmap. After polishing the core functions and effects for the recent teaser, we started with the real fun part of indie-gamedev: designing the first biome.


[h1]The Forest[/h1]

The first level needs to familiarize the player with the main mechanics, simple combat, some light puzzles, and plenty of fun character interactions that drive exploration and deliver story. For the forest we laid out a long stretch of meadows, caves, a lake-house, and dinosaurs with big ears; then filled it with props, items, and enemies.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40056258/a2c5b7ec2bbed0c5f0483e1a809ebc2c7abe179e.png[/img]

Creating these initial spaces is a chaotic time, since everything we try to introduce opens up more issues: a new room needs an obstacle, that needs some collision, that needs some visual feedback, that needs an effect-library, that needs sounds. You get the idea.

During these early days, the Ghost of map and UI haunts the whole production. It is the one thing every game developer hates and therefore tries to procrastinate until as late as possible — a lesson we learned painfully with Resolutiion.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40056258/3524572ef29344fd130c54d8de52eb370bc0eaac.png[/img]

Back on the bright side of the forest, each new biome is an opportunity for new, fun encounters: helpful NPCs, strange critters, and mean enemies are the pulsating beat of any video-game adventure. Here’s a small selection:

[h2]King Balal[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40056258/07c580e68d6d7f37c22c5cab923146869ed644bf.gif[/img]

The ruler of the Dung beetles tries to reach the heavens by building a large tower of dirt, up which he resides, ready to meet the supreme being.

[h2]The Shepherd[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40056258/a32663e97b1d9d2ecb1e72ddf6b1edd0b00c671b.gif[/img]

This steady scarecrow is our friendly guide to the wonders of the sky-island. He seems to know his way around and never shies from sharing his insights.

[h2]Unifox[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40056258/c0dbc633d349161b4e75c94c8ea68d507a2065f6.gif[/img]

Half fox, half unicorn. Unfortunately the deafening airships have made this little guy as angry as it is cute, so you’ll need to calm it down with a Stone’s Soul or two.


[h1]German Cumputer-Game Awards[/h1]

During hardcore development of Lila’s Sky Ark, something truly unexpected happened: Resolutiion got nominated for Germany’s Game Awards. We assume that there was some serious bribery involved by our publisher, but it must not have been enough — we didn’t win.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40056258/c6d69350da3f5a6883b292460ae95d2bd3c5d051.png[/img]

Still, being nominated for “Best Game design” with our first, twisted baby was surreal and entertaining. The whole (and honestly way too tame) [url=https://youtu.be/3HAxKj7Y72Y?t=3967]award-show can be found on YouTube[/url], but we doubt it’s worth anybody’s time, just to see various webcam-faces flicker by.

Maybe a bit more interesting is an [url=https://youtu.be/UxgBMfF1Lpk?t=4237]interview snipped with Günther[/url] from the pre-show, where GameStar asked us about the importance of such events as well as how we see Monolith of Mind’s development as a serious studio. Spoilers: we don’t do serious.


[h1]The Quality of Life & Death Update[/h1]

Almost twelve months ago we released Resolutiion. And boy, has it been a ride. Two major updates later (“The Red Plains” and “The Craftsman”) and we realized, that the journey of Valor and Alibii is not the end but a beginning. We wanted to tell a much grander story about humanity and technology; about death and rebirth.

To honor Resolutiion’s birthday, we took some time off our mad schedule, and collected a lot of feedback and bug fixes into the “Quality of Life & Death” Update:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40056258/0ccff810cd6e5060ff527f2d8af6d4c38d37d537.png[/img]

[list]
[*] various visual improvements,
[*] remarkably reduced loading times,
[*] earlier access to the fast-travel system (Theremin in Sunken City),
[*] tinted map for clearer orientation,
[*] progression changes, simplifying access to parts of the world,
[*] Issue 879: a new secret,
[*] bug fixes & general polish.
[/list]

Happy birthday, Valor and Alibii.
The update should be out in late May, so stay tuned.


[h2]Free Pizza[/h2]

To end this long and overdue newsletter, let us once more ask you to strengthen the ties than bind us: kindly [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1573390/Lilas_Sky_Ark/]wishlist Lila’s Sky Ark on Steam[/url] and [url=https://discord.gg/uAkZgBp7gz]join our Discord server[/url] for a slice of digital pizza. Having you around for the journey alone makes it worthwhile, and gets us motivated to write these lines every few weeks or so.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40056258/116e1b41ed4edd62e7382473255fc92259202bd3.png[/img]

Thanks for reading up until here.
Fell free to follow some links above and take care.

notes.title: Wake up, Lila
notes.notes:
Hey there, fellow pixel-lovers. It’s been a while since we took the time to write up a proper newsletter. We’ll make up for it by announcing our new game. But wait, a quick reminder why you are here: this is “Views from the Monolith,” Monolith of Minds’ infrequent newsletter about indie games, DIY development, and stories from magenta cyberspace. Great to have you around.

Between November and February we brainstormed, planned, and prototyped a new game. Progress is fun and mad, and we finally want to shout its name out into the world: drum roll, blast beats, and Japanese percussion please:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40056258/60bb5a02c1c9d0d98ce0d05b5a3b542087edd9fb.png[/img]

[h1]Lila’s Sky Ark[/h1]

“Lila and her friends — Mr. Kiepchen and Doctor-Father-Sir — wake up to find themselves facing a grim foe: The Conductor and his generals who have invaded the sky island to take all that is magical and musical. You must unite the spirits of the forest, the mountain, the sky, and the core to fight back! Defend your home with copper, bone, and alchemy against this fleet of deafening airships.”

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40056258/9535d6cd708f141085e2cc8798ddbbe18decdd34.png[/img]

We’ve already put together a [url=https://youtu.be/grcuPl9jjn0]short Teaser Trailer on YouTube[/url] and launched the [url=https://lilasskyark.monolithofminds.com/]game’s website[/url] with more info, screenshots, and an ambitious roadmap. You should be able to play an Early Access version of Lila’s Sky Ark in late summer of 2021.

One of the most enjoyable parts of game development is the interaction with past and future players. That’s why this time we decided to build our game in the open, as transparent as possible. Therefore we set up a [url=https://discord.gg/uAkZgBp7gz]Discord server[/url] and you’re invited! Sure, there will be spoilers, but life’s always about the journey, right? RIGHT?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40056258/f0a3f9e38df55b4d6c9dc66af11baba9a07e4488.png[/img]

Come say, “Hi.”
Show your work.
Enjoy the progress or just lurk.

[h2]Make a Wish[/h2]

With all the exciting links above, why are you still reading?

Well, then let us thank you for your patience and dismiss you with a final plea: like other indie devs, wishlisting on Steam is very important for any game’s ranking and recommendations. Therefore consider visiting [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1573390/Lilas_Sky_Ark/]Lila’s Steam Ark[/url], and click the button that says “Buy Pizza” or “Start a War” or whatever you need to do to stay in the loop.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40056258/4d106f8577099e5432c025606ca7663d9514effa.png[/img]

Thanks for reading.
See you on the island.
